Thanks for taking this on. Our auditors have flagged that we need a concrete, auditable process for transporting customer-managed keys (BYOK) into our air-gapped private deployment. Specifically they want: a signed attestation for chain-of-custody, precise operator roles during the physical transfer, and a network diagram showing the isolated staging environment.

Can Redwood produce a short checklist we can attach to the audit packet and walk through an operator rehearsal with our sysops team? We are planning the physical transfer the week of Feb 9 — hoping to lock details this month.

- Is an HSM-backed seal required or is KMS-wrapped key import acceptable?

Alice — thanks, and noted on the Feb 9 window. I put together a compact checklist (attached) and sketched responsibilities below so you can include them in the audit packet. Happy to run a dry-run with your sysops.

High-level recommendation (short answer): HSM-backed import is preferred for the highest assurance. KMS-wrapped import can be accepted if the wrapped key is created under your KMS and we perform an HSM unwrap inside the air-gapped HSM during handoff.

Quick checklist (summary):
- Pre-flight (2 weeks out): share inventory and serials, confirm hardware attestation method, confirm operator list and 2-person rule for unseal/unwrap.
- Transport: tamper-evident packaging, dedicated courier + chain-of-custody form (signed at pick-up/drop-off).
- Handoff in staging SCIF: presence of both customer operator and Redwood witness, hardware attestation (HSM log extract), offline unwrap with HSM, immediate wrap under target HSM partition, no network connectivity during unwrap.
- Post-handoff: generate audit token (signed attestation), ledger entry in audit bucket, snapshot of HSM event log, and optional live verification via one-way checksum over an out-of-band channel.

Attachments I included: attestation-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — usable as the audit packet insert; docsign-byo-agreement.pdf — template Redwood uses for acceptance/sign-off.

Open questions for your sysops:
- Can your team provide a second operator for the two-person rule?
- Do you require the unwrap to be performed on an HSM-certified appliance (FIPS 140-2/3)?
- Will the staging facility accept courier + sign-off or do we need an escorted transfer?

Next steps: if you confirm the two-person operator and facility constraints, Marcus will outline the minimal network/host controls for the staging environment and I can schedule a 60-minute rehearsal.

— Olga
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding operational constraints and a minimal network diagram for the staging area. I attached a small diagram for reference. Key points:

- Network posture: staging host must be isolated from prod and have no outbound egress. If a verification channel is required, use a one-way data diode or physically separate verification laptop that never connects to the HSM network.
- Jump host: only a single, air-gapped jump host for operator consoles. No removable media is allowed except sealed, logged devices used only for key transport (tamper-evident USBs are acceptable if your policy permits).
- HSM partitioning: create a dedicated partition for the Acme key, with operator ACLs limited to wrap/unwrap actions. Operator accounts should be temporary and time-boxed.
- Evidence artifacts: HSM event logs, signed attestation (format in our spreadsheet), chain-of-custody PDF signed by both parties, and an MD5/SHA256 checksum published to your external compliance bucket (out-of-band).
- Rehearsal: recommend a canary run using a test key and a full end-to-end checklist. Plan 2-hour window; have both operators and an on-call Redwood engineer present.

Attachment: acme-airgap-network-diagram.png (png) — minimal staging topology.

If Acme wants a KMS-wrapped path instead of full HSM import, we can accept wrapped keys created under your KMS provided the unwrap happens inside our HSM with the same operator controls; documentation path will expand by one page in the checklist.

— Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
